# Requirements Quality Checklist: Authentication and Bootstrap Administration

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency and measurable coverage of identity/access, first-admin enrollment, storage/recovery, UX and operability requirements before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-10-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth / Audience**: Standard-depth reviewer/PR gate for inventory 005.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are production provider trust, verified login evidence and rejection without development/anonymous fallback fully specified independently of any particular identity vendor? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001/002/015/019; §US1]
- [ ] CHK002 Are stable external-to-internal identity requirements complete for concurrent first login, profile changes, distinct issuer/subject pairs and restart, without implicit account linking? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003; §US1.2/3; §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all first-admin ceremony states and operator/nominee responsibilities defined, including explicit authorization, expiry, replacement before consumption, atomic enrollment and permanent closure afterward? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010-012; §US2; Operator contract §Nominate and enroll]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the public/protected interface inventory complete for browser, direct API, trusted module, operator, safe health and environment-restricted contract publication, with ownership and access requirements stated for each? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005/007/021; §Interfaces and Permission Parity; Identity contract §Endpoint inventory]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the distinction between external login evidence, the admitted local API credential, internal actor and permission authority unambiguous, including unsupported or mixed credential types? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002/006/007/021; Identity contract §Origin and credential boundary; §Trusted actor-v1]
- [ ] CHK006 Are finite session lifetimes, renewal, next-request revocation, restart and secret/key rotation effects explicitly distinguished from provider-wide sign-out or immediate upstream revocation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008/009; Identity contract §Finite budgets; Operator contract §Sessions, mode and keys]
- [ ] CHK007 Are nominee matching and one-time authorization defined by verified identity rather than email/profile/first arrival, with no ambiguous meaning of initial administrator or production versus development authority? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010-014; §Scope and Dependencies; §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK008 Are invalid input, unauthenticated access, insufficient authority, unavailable enrollment, admission refusal and unavailable/uncertain dependencies distinguishable through documented safe results rather than redirects, raw errors or success-shaped fallback? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006/015/018; Identity contract §Successful identity and errors]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are browser, direct-host and adapter requirements consistent for identity, allowed origins/destinations, request binding, caching and error/redirect semantics, without creating an alternate trust path? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004/007/008/020; Identity contract §CSRF and browser binding; §Next.js adapter contract]
- [ ] CHK010 Do default denial, self-scoped identity/sign-out and nominated enrollment remain consistent with first-admin designation granting no team membership, resource permission or offline maintenance authority? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005/007/010/021; §Interfaces and Permission Parity; Identity contract §Trusted actor-v1]
- [ ] CHK011 Are development requirements consistent across environment, exposure opt-in, listeners/origins, persisted identity/session transitions and UI labeling, with no production enrollment or fallback exception? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013/014/020; §US4; Operator contract §Strict configuration and production trust]
- [ ] CHK012 Do host identity ownership, explicit format upgrades and complete-set recovery preserve accepted module assignment/schema/file/history and privilege boundaries without implied cross-module atomicity or ordinary-serving migration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011/016; §Data Ownership and Compatibility; Plan §Preparation, runtime and recovery]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Do all five stories, 22 acceptance scenarios, FR-001-022 and SC-001-007 have explicit, independently assessable evidence expectations rather than only a login-screen or fabricated-principal proxy? [Measurability, Spec §Required Validation; §Success Criteria; Quickstart §Acceptance matrix]
- [ ] CHK014 Are enrollment success criteria precise about at least twenty simultaneous eligible attempts, three fresh host restarts, one designation/consumed ceremony/security record and zero unauthorized additional grants on each real provider? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011/017/022; §SC-002/006; Quickstart §Acceptance matrix, US2.4]
- [ ] CHK015 Are post-return UI timing and accessibility criteria objectively bounded, with provider/human time excluded, actual test-profile reporting and explicit width, text enlargement, keyboard/focus/announcement and automated-finding thresholds? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020; §SC-005; §Experience, Security and Operations; Identity contract §UI state contract]
- [ ] CHK016 Are privacy and durability acceptance criteria explicit about required protected authentication exchanges versus prohibited disclosure, covered public/private channels, correlated outcomes and no known-success claim for uncertain commits? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015/017/018; §SC-006/007; §Required Validation]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are primary, cancelled, rejected, unavailable and corrected-retry login flows specified with safe local return continuity and no endless redirect or unverifiable-login fallback? [Coverage, Spec §US1.1/4/5; §US5.4; §FR-015/020]
- [ ] CHK018 Are session expiry/sign-out, concurrent renewal/revocation, trust/mode changes and key loss/rotation addressed without stale browser identity, cached actor authority or an implicit identity-data reset? [Coverage, Spec §US3.4; §FR-009/014/015; Operator contract §Sessions, mode and keys]
- [ ] CHK019 Are absent/expired/replaced/consumed ceremony and administrator/IdP-loss scenarios specified separately, including explicit recovery that cannot promote the next login or mint another initial administrator? [Coverage, Spec §US2.1/3/5; §FR-010/012; Operator contract §Nominate and enroll; §Recovery and compatibility]
- [ ] CHK020 Are clean installation, accepted-foundation upgrade, idempotent preparation, corrupt/unavailable state and interrupted recovery specified for both providers with exact preservation of committed identity and unrelated module state? [Coverage, Spec §US5.1/2; §FR-016; §SC-006; Operator contract §Prepare and upgrade]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Are malformed/missing identity keys, wrong issuer/recipient/signing material, expired or foreign attempt binding, replay/duplicate callbacks, credential confusion and spoofed actor/proxy claims covered by explicit rejection requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases; §FR-002/003/007/008; Quickstart §Acceptance matrix, US1.3/4 and US3.1/2]
- [ ] CHK022 Are unsafe/encoded return destinations, forged cross-origin mutations, absent/null origin and callback-specific browser binding addressed without conflating legitimate provider return with an ordinary protected mutation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008/019/020; §Edge Cases; Identity contract §Endpoint inventory; §CSRF and browser binding]
- [ ] CHK023 Are finite input/state/rate capacities, expiration boundaries and over-limit refusals defined without silent eviction of another user's session, unbounded housekeeping or a budget that prevents the required enrollment contention? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009/011/019; Identity contract §Finite budgets; Data model §Entities and constraints]
- [ ] CHK024 Are loss of acknowledgement and interruption before/after database commits, secret-file delivery, key preparation and restore reconciliation specified with truthful partial-effect/durability states and safe explicit retry? [Coverage, Spec §US2.4; §US5.2; §FR-011/015/016/017; Operator contract §Prepare and upgrade; §Nominate and enroll; §Recovery and compatibility]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK025 Are provider destination/network trust, TLS/DNS/redirect constraints, response sizes, request/cache/key-refresh counts and timeouts finite and explicit, including controlled private-IdP support without a deployed TLS bypass? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001/015/019; Identity contract §Finite budgets; Operator contract §Strict configuration and production trust]
- [ ] CHK026 Are deliberate loading, signed-out, signed-in, expired, development and failure/retry requirements defined consistently for the minimal accessible journey, including secret entry, stale-content clearing and non-enumerating announcements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004/018/020; §Experience, Security and Operations; Identity contract §UI state contract]
- [ ] CHK027 Are durable security events versus bounded request diagnostics, retention/access/capacity, recording failure and low-cardinality correlation requirements specified without storing secrets, unnecessary profile data or an implied general audit service? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017-019; Data model §__kofte_identity_events; Operator contract §Evidence, retention and privacy]
- [ ] CHK028 Are startup, callback, local-operation, adapter, maintenance and housekeeping envelopes mutually consistent with inherited deadlines and the five-second UI outcome, without implicit retries or an unbounded provider dependency? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015/019; §SC-005; Plan §Technical Context; Identity contract §Finite budgets; Operator contract §Proposed stopped command grammar]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK029 Are accepted 001-004 dependencies and the necessary route/storage/recovery compatibility changes documented without treating legacy blanket denial or exact inventories as permission to remove equivalent safeguards? [Dependency, Spec §Scope and Dependencies; §Required Validation; Plan §Summary; §Preparation, runtime and recovery]
- [ ] CHK030 Are operator responsibilities for public origin/ingress, proxy trust, secret delivery/custody, protected key persistence, installation authority and stopped/quarantined recovery explicit for the supported single-instance profiles? [Assumption, Spec §FR-010/016/019; §Experience, Security and Operations; Operator contract §Strict configuration and production trust; §Recovery and compatibility]
- [ ] CHK031 Are independently configured protocol, separately compiled trusted-consumer, real both-provider, browser/accessibility, privacy and retained regression evidence obligations specified with honest exclusions, rather than inferred from design approval or existing unrelated passes? [Dependency, Spec §FR-022; §Required Validation; Quickstart §Required local and CI verification; §Delivered guide consumer]
- [ ] CHK032 Are new direct/transitive dependency provenance, license, supported-version and lock/adoption gates distinguished from the already approved design, without a mandatory identity vendor, cloud service or unreviewed package assumption? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions and Constitutional Review; Plan §Technical Context; ADR 0007 §Approval; Constitution §III/VI]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK033 Are versioned actor/current-identity compatibility and later 006/007 integration boundaries unambiguous, with no implied MCP, job, machine-credential or granular-authorization capability delivered by this slice? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007/021; §Interfaces and Permission Parity; Identity contract §Successful identity and errors; §Trusted actor-v1]
- [ ] CHK034 Is stale-backup reconciliation clearly distinguished from ordinary restart and known consumed enrollment, including historical uncertainty, compatible-version/old-binary refusal and the limits of rollback/security-state guarantees? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012/016; §Edge Cases; §Data Ownership and Compatibility; Operator contract §Recovery and compatibility]
- [ ] CHK035 Are locked intent, approved ADR decisions, historical Proposed planning statements, future implementation evidence and remaining human-owned gates explicitly distinguished without inventing a conflicting current approval or completion state? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions and Constitutional Review; Plan §Summary; ADR 0007 §Approval; Constitution §Delivery and Review Gates]
- [ ] CHK036 Do acceptance/release requirements preserve historical failed or unavailable checks as limitations, the exact later-feature/MVP boundary and explicit human acceptance, rather than treating checklist satisfaction or an intermediate merge as delivered behavior? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022; §Scope and Dependencies; §Required Validation; Constitution §XI/XII; §Delivery and Review Gates]
